primitives.name: Server-Side Simulation Engine
primitives.verbatim_quote: No vendor ships its simulation math to the browser; every engine is server-side, and the only client-side model code found in 16 tools is a percentile multiplier (Part VII).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S_{\\text{sim}}': 'dimensionless, simulation run count', 'E_{\\text{outcome}}': 'points, expected lineup score', 'T_{\\text{latency}}': 'seconds, time to simulate lineup'}
primitives.assumptions: Simulation results are generated exclusively on backend servers with no client-side computation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When $ T_{\text{latency}} > 100ms $, performance degradation affects real-time strategy adaptation.

layer2.mapping: Simulation kernel computes expected scores based on historical player performance and ownership data.
layer2.telemetry: Average simulated lineup score variance and latency per simulation.

primitives.name: Millionaire Maker Entry Fee
primitives.verbatim_quote: Week 1 ran as a **$5-entry** NFL $3.5M Fantasy Football Millionaire with **832,342 entries**; the guarantee then stepped down $3.5M → $3M → $2.75M → $2.5M across the eight weeks.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'F_{\\text{entry}}': 'USD, entry fee', 'P_{\\text{guarantee}}': 'USD, guaranteed prize pool', 'N_{\\text{week}}': 'dimensionless, week number'}
primitives.assumptions: Entry fees and prize pools scale inversely with contest popularity and risk exposure.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When $ F_{\text{entry}} < \$5 $, participation rate increases beyond threshold.

layer2.mapping: Entry fee structure mirrors a risk-reward utility function across contest weeks.
layer2.telemetry: Total entries per week and corresponding entry fee changes.
